---
title: "Lectures on Causal Panel Analysis"
subtitle: "Yiqing Xu, Stanford University"
---

Slides for six lectures of 100 to 120 minutes each on causal inference with panel data. The
lectures are for applied researchers and graduate students in the social sciences who work with
panel data. Each method is introduced through an example and a picture, and formulas appear only
where the ideas need them.

| # | Lecture | Slides | Source |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | The Parametric Approach | [52 pp](https://yiqingxu.org/public/panel-lectures/handout/Xu_1parametric_handout.pdf) | [code](https://github.com/xuyiqing/panel-lectures/tree/main/01-parametric) |
| 2 | Difference-in-Differences | [47 pp](https://yiqingxu.org/public/panel-lectures/handout/Xu_2did_handout.pdf) | [code](https://github.com/xuyiqing/panel-lectures/tree/main/02-did) |
| 3 | Factorial Difference-in-Differences | [39 pp](https://yiqingxu.org/public/panel-lectures/handout/Xu_3fdid_handout.pdf) | [code](https://github.com/xuyiqing/panel-lectures/tree/main/03-fdid) |
| 4 | Two-Way Fixed Effects Revisited | [33 pp](https://yiqingxu.org/public/panel-lectures/handout/Xu_4twfe_handout.pdf) | [code](https://github.com/xuyiqing/panel-lectures/tree/main/04-twfe) |
| 5 | Modern DID | [48 pp](https://yiqingxu.org/public/panel-lectures/handout/Xu_5modern_handout.pdf) | [code](https://github.com/xuyiqing/panel-lectures/tree/main/05-modern) |

The page counts link to the PDFs, which have one page per slide. To present with the step-by-step
reveals, build that version from the LaTeX source (`make animated`). "Code" opens the
lecture's folder on GitHub: the LaTeX source, the figures, and the R scripts that draw them.

## The arc

Lectures 1 and 2 cover the parametric panel toolkit and the canonical difference-in-differences
design. Lecture 3 extends that design to events that affect everyone (factorial
difference-in-differences). Lecture 4 diagnoses three problems with two-way fixed effects: the
design problem (what strict exogeneity implies for treatment assignment), violations of parallel
trends, and the weighting problem when effects differ across units. Lecture 5 repairs the
weighting problem with estimators that allow effects to differ, and works through three
applications from a large reanalysis study. Lecture 6 turns to synthetic control, factor models,
and doubly and triply robust estimators, which handle some violations of parallel trends.

::: {.lead-note}
The field is moving fast, and these slides lean toward the author's own research and
understanding of it. Read them as one path through the material rather than as a survey.
:::

## Software

The R packages used in the lectures, with tutorials:

- [fect](https://yiqingxu.org/packages/fect/): fixed effects counterfactual estimators.
- [gsynth](https://yiqingxu.org/packages/gsynth/): the generalized synthetic control method.
- [fdid](https://yiqingxu.org/packages/fdid/): factorial difference-in-differences.
- [panelView](https://yiqingxu.org/packages/panelView/): visualizing panel data.
